cards.text: Zechariah is a prophet to God's people, and they're rebuilding the house of God in Jerusalem with Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest (Zechariah 1:1; Haggai 1:1; Ezra 5:1-2). He's just seen four chariots ride out in a vision (Zechariah 6:1-8), and now the word of the LORD comes to him again. No horses this time, friend, just a TO-DO LIST.

Step one: take an offering from three exiles who have arrived from Babylon: Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah. Babylon to Jerusalem is a LONG road, friend. The longest trip I ever took was across the Millers' kitchen, and it ended in a JUNK DRAWER.

cards.question: Zechariah's next stop is the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah. True or false: God tells him to go there that same day.

cards.text: Next, God tells Zechariah to take silver and gold and make something ornate. Me? I spent YEARS under takeout menus in a junk drawer, and NOBODY ever called me ornate.

cards.question: God's plan for that silver and gold: make an ornate ___.
God says to set the ornate silver and gold crown on the head of the high priest. Whose head is that?

cards.text: So the crown goes on Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Then Zechariah is to tell him what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Here is a man whose name is the Branch, and He will branch out from His place…'

cards.question: God's people are rebuilding right now. So what will the man called the Branch do? He will build the ___ of the LORD.

cards.text: Then it comes AGAIN: 'Yes, He will build the temple of the LORD; He will be clothed in splendor and will sit on His throne and rule.' When I repeat myself it's because I forgot, but when God repeats Himself, friend, you LEAN IN.

cards.question: The Branch will sit on His throne and rule. What else will He be, right there on that throne?
The Branch will sit on His throne and rule, and He'll be a priest on His throne. Then God speaks of the two. What will there be between them?

cards.text: The crown becomes a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah and the gracious son of Zephaniah. The Millers carved MY name into my handle, but these folks get remembered with a CROWN, so same idea, WAY shinier.

cards.question: That memorial crown has to live somewhere. Where does it stay?

answers.text: In the temple of the LORD

cards.text: Then the message turns to the crew who will build the temple of the LORD. My whole bakery runs on invitations, friend, so I am VERY interested in who's on this crew.

cards.question: True or false: people from far away will come and build the temple of the LORD.

cards.text: And here's the next line: 'you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you.' But hold up, friend, because there's an IF.

cards.question: God's message to Zechariah ends with an IF. What does it say?

answers.text: If you diligently obey the LORD's voice
If you faithfully keep the Sabbath day
If you gladly give your silver and gold

findings.problem: The opening already identifies Joshua as the high priest. When card 6 later asks which named man is the high priest on whose head the crown is set, that earlier identification makes Joshua son of Jehozadak identifiable as the correct option before the question.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the offering instruction, the observation about the road from Babylon to Jerusalem, and the junk-drawer punchline. It needs to be shortened to two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the silver and gold will be made into something ornate. It gives no basis for reasoning out a crown rather than a lampstand or an altar, so the blank asks for an unseen detail instead of testing meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
